newsitem.title: USA: Barrick ups Pascua reserves, Pierina to mine.
newsitem.headline: Barrick ups Pascua reserves, Pierina to mine.

text.p: Barrick Gold Corp said on Wednesday that it increased reserves at its Pascua mine in Chile by 18 percent to 7.7 million ounces of gold.
The world's third largest gold producer also said its initial estimates for its Pierina gold property in Peru were conservative and that it plans to elevate Pierina to mine development.

Senior Barrick executives told the Denver Gold Show that "Barrick's gold production will rise significantly by the year 2000 as a result of these new reserves," the Toronto-based firm said in a statement.
Initial production of the Pascua Mine, located in Barrick's El Indio Property in Chile, is forecast in the range of 400,000 ounces, it said.
Reserves may still rise at Pascua since the ore body is still open in some areas, it said.
Alan Hill, Barrick's executive vice-president of development, also discussed Pierina's production estimates.

"The initial production estimate for Pierina is 500,000 ounces of gold per year, beginning in 1999. Costs should be below US$100 an ounce, due in part to a substantial silver by-product credit," Hill said.
Barrick bought Arequipa Resources Ltd and the Pierina property for C$915 million in late August.
Barrick's purchase of Arequipa included close to 50 other Peruvian gold properties. "We expect that these properties have the potential to host other Pierinas," it said.
